
The `russell_eligible_band` step applies the documented $30 million minimum capitalization to the ranked universe. The `russell_hci_band` step additionally admits foreign-incorporated companies with US headquarters under the reconstructed home-country criterion. These operational choices aim to construct the Russell universe required by AGK's banding control; they are supported by the bridge's recorded methodology justification, not specified in that detail by AGK. Unavailable float and voting eligibility screens are not silently treated as implemented.

The `prior_absent_indicator` step separates absence from the prior Russell file from Russell 1000 membership rather than assigning both the same zero. The `prior_recon_t1` step then reads the prior control and its interaction from reconstitution year t−1, as implied by AGK's definition of R2000 for “reconstitution year t” (draft p. 18). Finally, `stock_mktcap_poly` changes the polynomial argument from company capitalization to the event stock's own CRSP May capitalization. Table 2 defines Mktcap as the market value of equity of “stock i measured at May 31 in year t” (draft p. 39); two events without that stock-level value leave on complete case rather than receiving an undocumented fallback.

The other recorded variants measure an additional absent-by-band interaction, an earlier company-level CRSP polynomial replacement, name linking without the date-spell restriction, a banding indicator from Russell's May cross-section, same-year campaign collapse, a September-to-September campaign window, stock-level float, and the broader passive measure. None is suppressed because its coefficient moves away from AGK. The earlier six-axis diagnosis separately varies cohorts, rank construction, ownership classification and denominator, reporting-date conventions, controls and clustering, and published comparison measures. On its original baseline, the controls reduce the firm-year raw passive contrast from 2.74 to 0.85 pp and explain 87.2% of index-assignment variance. Removing reported controls raises the coefficient, but does not reproduce AGK's specification. These are baseline diagnostics, not bounds on the later reconstructed first stage.

## C. Remaining discrepancies and construction caveats

The final event-grain active coefficient, −1.722 pp (SE 3.924), lies within one AGK standard error of 1.670. Unclassified ownership remains −1.571 pp (SE 0.956), which is 1.09 pp below the lower edge of AGK's one-standard-error band, −0.476, and about 1.9 of our standard errors below AGK's point estimate. Passive ownership is 2.619 pp (SE 1.089) at the event grain and 2.779 pp (SE 0.331) at the firm-year grain, versus AGK's event-grain 4.292 pp (SE 1.111). We do not describe this as a complete first-stage replication. In particular, the event estimate is already inside AGK's 95% interval; the remaining discrepancy is in the magnitude, not a rejection of equality at that confidence level.

The prior-absent indicator has an exclusion-like effect at the event grain. At its introduction, it marks five rows at four companies, all additions from outside the Russell 3000. Its effect is numerically equivalent to deleting those rows for unclassified and passive ownership and accounts for two thirds of the deletion effect on active ownership. None of the marked rows is more than two standard deviations from the active-ownership mean. They constitute a membership category that AGK's “unless” clause does not address, rather than extreme observations, so the text supports separating them; nevertheless, the event-grain effect deserves no more weight than an exclusion. In the firm-year sample, the indicator marks 73 rows and behaves like an ordinary control, moving active ownership by only +0.18 pp. These counts describe the introduction of the indicator, before the later prior-reconstitution recoding.

The treatment of float and polynomial grain is asymmetric. AGK's stock-level language supports both readings, but we adopt the stock-level polynomial and refuse the `stock_float` variant because it moves active ownership outside the one-standard-error band, to −2.296 pp (SE 3.905), and moves unclassified ownership farther away, to −1.648 pp (SE 1.035). Passive ownership becomes 2.391 pp (SE 1.247) at the event grain and 1.808 pp at the firm-year grain. The headline therefore mixes a stock-level polynomial with a company-level, Russell-implied float, chosen partly on the non-passive legs. The stock-float variant uses the share-class block-adjusted June float, so the comparison should not be read as an exact source-invariant change of aggregation grain. Both variants are reported in Table A2.

One Hubbell campaign illustrates event-level sensitivity to share-class selection. Replacing its own event stock, PERMNO 32942, with the company-year representative, PERMNO 32934, changes only that event's polynomial and moves the quadratic active coefficient by +1.40 pp and the unclassified coefficient by +0.44 pp. Unclassified ownership remains below AGK's one-standard-error band. The residual 1.09 pp shortfall is therefore within the scale of effects that unresolved event-level data choices can generate, but this diagnostic does not establish AGK's share-class choice. Their text specifies stock i, so we retain the own-stock reading; source vintage and historical share-class selection remain unresolved.

## D. Fund composition and broader passive ownership

The benchmark-composition diagnostic measures a Russell-benchmarked share of fund-passive ownership of 20.7% at the event grain and 19.5% at the firm-year grain on covered band observations. At the measured per-dollar intensities, the corresponding shares needed to produce AGK's magnitude are approximately 41.7% and 41.5%. These implied shares are design-free composition arithmetic on covered rows, not estimates of AGK's actual fund composition or a calibrated replacement first stage. The underlying roll-call covers 173 of 457 events and 2,598 of 6,617 firm-years. Its full-frame regression decomposition assigns zero Russell share outside coverage, making that component a lower bound; we do not interpret the resulting full-frame shares as population composition.

Holdings provide a separate check on index labels. Russell 2000 trackers hold 90.5–100% of Russell 2000-labeled band companies and at most 0.66% of Russell 1000-labeled companies; Russell 1000 trackers show the corresponding opposite pattern. Among Russell-benchmarked funds, the band-local Russell 2000/Russell 1000 passive-dollar ratio ranges from 6.62 to 10.16 across cohorts. Non-Russell broad index funds have ratios of only 0.90–1.19. Their substantial holdings on both sides dilute the aggregate fund-passive contrast without implying that the Russell treatment labels are reversed. These funds remain passive under AGK's classification, so dropping them to increase λ would change the measure being replicated.

Widening the ownership measure gives a different result. Under the `russell_hci_band` controls, the recorded `hidden_passive` firm-year estimate for passive_all is 3.666 pp (SE 0.457), compared with the fund-only estimate of 1.662 pp (SE 0.325). The broader estimate lies inside AGK's 95% interval, [2.114, 6.470], and is approximately 85% of their point estimate. Its passive-ownership mean is 17.894%, rather than the fund-only 9.221%, so this is deliberately not an adopted AGK replication step. The broader measure counts passive assets absent from S12, including the Form 5500 CIT component and the separately managed account component represented in the recorded hidden/modeled leg.

That estimate uses the earlier `russell_hci_band` controls, and at the event grain it is only 2.264 pp (SE 1.844). Table A3 re-estimates both measures under the final `stock_mktcap_poly` controls on identical rows. The widened source lacks one firm-year (recon year 2011, PERMCO 11023), so the firm-year comparison drops it from both measures; the fund-only estimate on the full 6,617 rows is 2.779 pp (SE 0.331), which differs from the harmonized estimate only in the third decimal. The event sample loses no rows.

Under the final controls, adding the CIT and separately managed components raises the quadratic estimate from 2.619 to 3.370 pp at the event grain and from 2.777 to 5.582 pp at the firm-year grain. Both passive_all estimates lie inside AGK's 95% interval. The event estimate is 79% of AGK's 4.292 but imprecise, since its standard error of 1.734 exceeds the 0.751 pp gain over fund-only. The firm-year estimate is 130% of AGK's point estimate and roughly double the fund-only estimate, in proportion to mean ownership, which also roughly doubles (the ratio of coefficient to mean is 0.31 for passive_all and 0.30 for fund-only). At the event grain the added ownership carries a smaller discontinuity per unit of mean (0.19 against 0.30). The ordering holds at every polynomial order. These estimates show that passive assets outside S12 carry a Russell discontinuity of their own; they do not show that AGK's S12 measure contained those assets, and they leave the fund-only shortfall at the event grain unresolved.

## E. Second-stage results

The second-stage CSV records an earlier, separate estimation and is not a refit of the final sample and control bridge. For seeking board representation, the calendar-window, quadratic event specification contains 206 events at 146 firms. With both the outcome and endogenous ownership scaled by their own sample standard deviations, the just-identified IV coefficient is −0.677 (SE 1.831) for fund passive and −0.374 (SE 0.950) for passive_all; the common reduced form is −0.130 (SE 0.370). In percentage-point ownership units the coefficients are −0.177 and −0.068, respectively. The difference in these IV estimates reflects the inverse ratio of the first stages on the same rows, rather than independent reduced-form evidence for two effects. Both 95% Anderson–Rubin confidence sets are the whole real line. These estimates use CRV1 clustering by firm, ownership/reconstitution years 2007–2013, campaign years 2008–2014, and polynomial order 2, as recorded in `data/output/agk2019_second_stage.csv`. They do not provide a precise causal estimate or establish replication of AGK's second stage.
